source_verification_receipts.version: accepted author manuscript corresponding to JASA DOI 10.1080/01621459.2018.1469990; publisher Version of Record access was blocked
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited paper states strict positivity, a lower bound on actual survivor-complier probability, Z-based selection monotonicity, and treatment monotonicity conditional on always-selection; its exclusion is a conditional mean restriction among always-selected units.

Full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary-bootstrap consistency with a Gaussian first-stage limit, and the paper proposes an alternative resampling scheme for directional derivatives.
The paper extends scalar partially identified confidence intervals to vector-valued parameters and applies when asymptotically normal upper- and lower-bound estimates are available.
The paper derives sharp symbolic nonparametric bounds for ordinal probability-of-benefit, no-harm, and relative-treatment-effect measures in observational and imperfect-randomized settings.
For pure moment inequalities, numerous partial-identification regularity assumptions essentially coincide with the Mangasarian–Fromowitz constraint qualification.
The paper proves pointwise root-n LP-value inference, unrestricted uniform-consistency impossibility, and uniform consistency under a stated minimal restriction.
The paper gives scale-free Gaussian-maximum density bounds, while its uniform all-quantile consequence requires the largest marginal variance to be separated from zero.
